title: Calves
summary: The gastrocnemius (the visible two-headed calf) and the soleus underneath. Both point the foot; only the gastrocnemius crosses the knee. Standing raises grew the gastrocnemius far more than seated raises, and the bottom (stretched) half of the raise grew it most.

what_it_is.overview: The app splits calves into two map regions: gastrocnemius and soleus. Weekly targets count both together.

heads.name: Gastrocnemius, medial head
heads.origin: The back of the inner thigh bone, just above the knee.
heads.insertion: The heel bone, through the Achilles tendon.
heads.fiber_direction: Runs down the inner calf; the bigger of the two heads.

heads.name: Gastrocnemius, lateral head
heads.origin: The back of the outer thigh bone, just above the knee.
heads.insertion: The heel bone, through the Achilles tendon.

heads.name: Soleus
heads.origin: The back of the upper shin and fibula.
heads.insertion: The heel bone, through the Achilles tendon.
heads.fiber_direction: Broad, flat muscle under the gastrocnemius, visible at the sides of the lower calf.

what_it_does.action: Plantarflexion (pointing the foot, rising onto the toes).
what_it_does.detail: The job in every calf raise and jump.
Why bent-knee raises slacken the gastrocnemius.

what_it_does.action: Grew far more in standing (knee straight) than seated raises.
what_it_does.detail: Lateral head 12.4% vs 1.7%, medial 9.2% vs 0.6% over 12 weeks; soleus growth was similar either way.

synergists.name: Deep calf muscles and peroneals
synergists.role: Help point the foot; not tracked.

stabilizer_roles.text: In regular squats and lunges the calves steady the ankle; rated below 0.25 for calves.
Jumps load the calves hard and fast; jumps are rated 0.4 to 0.5.

relationships.indirect_note: Each working set adds the exercise's rating for this muscle to the weekly total, and ratings under 0.25 count as 0. 4 sets of standing calf raise (1.0), 3 sets of seated calf raise (1.0) and 3 sets of box jump (0.4) give 4 + 3 + 1.2 = 8.2, which the panel shows as 8 (rounded to the nearest 0.5). The full list comes live from exercises.json; the rows above are examples and the ratings are coaching estimates.

how.stretch_position: Heel dropped below the step at the bottom.
how.stance: Standing, Smith machine or leg-press calf raise.

bias.caveat: Knee-straight raises keep the gastrocnemius long at the knee. The map rates these gastrocnemius 1.0.

how.stretch_position: Deep heel drop; pause in the stretch; partials in the bottom half late in a set.

bias.caveat: Bottom-half partials grew the medial gastrocnemius 15.2% vs 6.7% for full range and 3.4% for top-half partials in 8 weeks (young women).
Soleus growth was similar seated or standing, so seated raises add soleus work but little gastrocnemius growth.

how.stance: Leg-press or seated calf raise instead of a loaded standing raise.

bias.caveat: Standing and Smith raises carry the 'Spinal loading' flag.

best_exercises.why: Knee straight with a deep heel drop; grew the gastrocnemius far more than seated raises.
Same knee-straight position, easy to load; stretch-biased in the app.
Knee-straight raise without load on the spine.
Soleus work with the knee bent; gastrocnemius rated 0.4 on the map.

mistakes.text: Bouncing out of the bottom, so the stretched range gets no controlled work.
Bending the knees on standing raises so the quads help.

coach_cues.cue: Drop the heel all the way, pause, then rise.
coach_cues.why: Uses the stretched range, where the extra growth was seen.
Keeps the gastrocnemius long at the knee.
Keeps the ankle from rolling out.

notes: Weekly target in the app: 6 to 16 calves sets at Advanced. Intermediate and Beginner scale the minimum by 0.8 and 0.6; the maximum stays the same. Render the numbers from targets.json, not from this text.
